solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A quartet in speech with a model prediction

indicators.note: in speech means the number for a quartet is to be heard, not read, giving a golf-shout spelling

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four
a cast is a model or mould taken of something

explanation.surface: A forecaster's four voices team up with a fashion model to make a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' turns FOUR into its soundalike FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what is expected to happen, a straightforward synonym for a prediction.

clue.text: Endless record on your old foul

indicators.note: Endless tells us to cut the final letter off the word for record

parts.note: a file is a record kept on something
thy is the old, archaic form of your

explanation.surface: An unfinished record of your old misdeeds turns out foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last E of FILE to leave FIL; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy and foul are synonyms for something dirty, disgusting or obscene.

clue.text: Land of Hope? I ruin a rat on the run

indicators.note: on the run suggests letters scattering in flight, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rat-catcher in a hopeful land boasts of ruining a fleeing rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Hope' looks like the patriotic song, but it is the novelist Anthony Hope, who invented this kingdom in The Prisoner of Zenda; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary central European kingdom created by the writer Anthony Hope.

clue.text: Reddy-brown deer reported in oily sea foam

parts.note: chocolate is a reddish-brown colour

indicators.note: reported signals that the deer's name is heard rather than spelt, giving a soundalike

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A reddish-brown deer is said to be seen in oily foam at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns MOOSE into the dessert-word MOUSSE; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil spills whipped by waves form a brown water-in-oil emulsion that marine scientists nickname after the dessert.

clue.text: Official to worry over a road

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the first word sits above the rest

parts.note: to stew is to worry or fret

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat frets about a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who manages events, races or property.

clue.text: Avoid cut after escape

indicators.note: after places the word for cut behind the abbreviation for escape

parts.note: ESC is the escape key on a keyboard
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid getting cut after a jailbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately keep away from it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Imminent issue forced union

parts.note: issue means offspring: a baby on the way forced the couple to wed

explanation.surface: A coming dispute pushes a trade union into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests industrial relations; 'issue' is a child and 'union' a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This hasty wedding is one arranged because the bride is pregnant, supposedly with her father holding a firearm.

clue.text: Tug's energy in hold

indicators.note: in places the physics letter for energy inside the word for hold

parts.note: to have is to hold or possess
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tugboat's power is kept in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to pull hard, much as a tug is a strong pull.

clue.text: Specially arranged rag week around clubs remains

indicators.note: around means the reshuffled letters enclose the card-suit letter
specially arranged indicates the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A student charity week specially laid on around nightclubs leaves debris behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British student fundraising week of stunts. 'Specially arranged' makes WREKAGE of RAG WEEK, and 'around' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is what remains after something is destroyed, the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Do Morse? A policeman initially involved with spiv

indicators.note: involved with means the first pieces are wrapped up inside the word for a spiv

parts.note: a tout is a shady seller, like a spiv, a British term for a black-market wheeler-dealer

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word policeman

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse has a policeman tangled up with a spiv.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse looks like the TV detective, but it is the telegraph code; 'involved with' puts A and P inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code messages are tapped out on a key, so sending one is to tap out.

clue.text: Boat on lake's broad and slow

indicators.note: on means the boat's name comes after the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: L is a standard map abbreviation for lake
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A boat on a lake is wide and sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical tempo marking literally means broad and indicates a very slow, stately pace.

clue.text: Pontificate on English test centre? It's complicated

indicators.note: on puts the word for pontificate after the other pieces in this across clue

parts.note: a lab is a place where tests are carried out
to orate is to speak pompously, to pontificate

explanation.surface: Sounding off about an English exam venue is a complicated business.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and detailed, a synonym for complicated.

clue.text: An awkward subject breaking news before King Edward?

indicators.note: before places the word for breaking news ahead of the vegetable

parts.note: breaking news is hot, fresh off the press
King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A tricky story breaks ahead of the King's announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks royal but is a potato variety; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a controversial issue that nobody wants to handle, as if it were too hot to hold.

clue.text: European runs in anorak?

indicators.note: in places the cricket abbreviation inside the slang word for an anorak

parts.note: anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a geek
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A European goes jogging in a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' suggests a coat but is British slang for a nerdy obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a European, being a native of Greece.

clue.text: Popular loch also away from the coast

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
L is the abbreviation for a loch or lake
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A popular Scottish loch also lies well away from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland describes places in the interior of a country, distant from the shore.

clue.text: Guy's securing correct pet with gent

indicators.note: correct as a verb means fix or put right, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Guy restrains a well-behaved pet alongside a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a man's name but is a guy rope; 'correct' rearranges PET GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg is driven into the ground to anchor the rope holding a tent upright.

clue.text: Operetta's spoiled by my libretto?

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lyricist confesses that a light opera was ruined by his own words.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the confession of an inferior versifier, while 'spoiled' rearranges OPERETTAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of inferior verse, the sort who would ruin an operetta's words.

clue.text: Repros inside to get refurbed

indicators.note: refurbed means refurbished or done up, so the letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Reproductions inside are going to be refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Repros are reproductions, and editions are copies issued of a book or print.

clue.text: Cartoonist's bloomers?

parts.note: bloomers are both blunders and women's underwear; cartoonists are people who draw

explanation.surface: A cartoonist makes some embarrassing blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Cartoonists draw, so they are drawers; bloomers are old-fashioned knickers, another meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people who draw and an old term for knickers or bloomers.

clue.text: Covering where ships finally moor

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of the word ships

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land, a moor

explanation.surface: A shelter where vessels at last tie up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' looks like tying up a boat but is open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover, such as one for a blade.

clue.text: A jungle with diamonds gets knocked for six

parts.note: a jungle is a confusing tangle, a maze
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Someone in a jungle with diamonds is bowled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked for six' is a British idiom from cricket, a ball hit for six runs, meaning stunned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knocked for six means being overwhelmed with astonishment, a synonym for being astonished.

clue.text: Trouper in part is terrific

indicators.note: in signals the answer is concealed within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A performer playing a role is brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, as a trouper is a seasoned performer.

clue.text: The sort of hopeful punt non-specialist includes

indicators.note: includes signals that the answer sits inside the word before it

explanation.surface: An amateur gambler places a hopeful bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on spec means doing it speculatively, without a firm order or guarantee.

clue.text: A whiff inside to ban

indicators.note: inside puts the first pieces within the word to

parts.note: taken as written
BO is body odour, an unpleasant whiff

explanation.surface: An unpleasant smell inside leads to a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social or cultural prohibition, so it serves as a ban.

clue.text: Two-legged beast's tender boxing exercises?

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the exercise letters are put inside the offer

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as a bid is an offer
PE is physical education, exercises at school

explanation.surface: A creature on two legs has sore muscles from boxing workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like sore but is an offer; 'boxing' is enclosing, not fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped is any animal that walks on two legs.

clue.text: Please go in home following thanks

indicators.note: following places the word for home after the word for thanks

parts.note: to enter is to go in
ta is British informal for thanks
in means at home

explanation.surface: Please come in to my home, with thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to amuse or delight them, which is to please them.

clue.text: Colleague locates counters

parts.note: oppo is British informal for a colleague or partner
sites as a verb means places or locates

explanation.surface: A colleague finds where the counters are.
explanation.definitionFit: Counters are things that oppose or contrast, as in arguments set against one another.

clue.text: A cold ram is to malfunction

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cold sheep is going to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: When a machine is acting up it is playing up or failing to work properly.

clue.text: I ignored the aforementioned dive to get down

indicators.note: ignored means the letter I is left out of the word for aforementioned

parts.note: said, as in 'the said person', means the aforementioned
a dive is a seedy bar or den

explanation.surface: Ignoring the earlier warning about a dive leaves one feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes I from SAID to leave SAD; 'dive' is a seedy haunt, not a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone down is to depress them, making them unhappy.

clue.text: Erotic dances with me first getting spectacular

indicators.note: first means the word me goes at the front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Erotic dancing with me in the lead becomes a spectacular show.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoric rise is dazzlingly rapid and brilliant, like a shooting star.
